That’s a fair observation! If your objects are flat with just a dozen fields, the reflection overhead in default System.Text.Json is already pretty low, so source generation’s advantage (e.g., the 90% speedup from the article) won’t be as pronounced. It really excels with complex, deeply nested objects where reflection costs nested up. For your scenario, the issue might not be serialization—try profiling to see if I/O or business logic is the real thing. play with JsonSerializerOptions (e.g., ignoring nulls) or adding RecyclableMemoryStream for streaming might still help a bit.
